articleTitle: Model of scandium doped aluminum nitride based PMUT with high transmitting performance
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (PMUT) model with high transmitting performance is established. 30% concentration scandium doped aluminum nitride film is used as piezoelectric material for the established MEMS model of PMUT. The expressions of PMUT vibration modes are given. The influence of PMUT structure on its transmitting sensitivity and receiving sensitivity is calculated. Through the frequency response of PMUT in medium, the influence of top electrode radius on resonant modes and transmitting parameters of PMUT is analyzed. Results show that (0,1) mode work in omni-directional mode, (0,2) mode operating in hypercardioid mode, and reasonable control of top electrode radius can be effective for designing target uses of PMUT.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of CTGS and YCOB crystals for high temperature piezoelectric accelerometer applications
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the compression model and shear model for high temperature piezoelectric accelerometer based on the CTGS and YCOB crystal cuts were studied. Based on the piezoelectric equation, the sensitivities (S) of the compression-mode and shear-mode accelerometer were derived and results shown that sensitivities S were affected by the piezoelectric constants d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub>/d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26</sub>/d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub> both for the compression-mode and shear-mode accelerometers. Temperature dependence of the piezoelectric constants was studied from room temperature to 800°C by the impedance analyzer, and the optimum crystal cuts with larger piezoelectric constant and good temperature stability were designed. It was found that for YCOB crystals, the variations of effective piezoelectric d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub> and d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26</sub> could be optimized to be <;5%, while for CTGS crystals, only the effective piezoelectric d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26</sub> can be optimized to <;7% over the whole temperature range. These results are helpful for designing high temperature piezoelectric accelerometers based on the CTGS and YCOB crystals.

articleTitle: Weighting technique for detection and location of targets by time reversal-reverse time migration mixed method
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Weighting technique is applied to detection and location of targets using the time reversal-reverse time migration mixed method and obtain the better focusing effect. In this paper, two different weighting techniques are weighting of distance between emission and reverence element and time-gate weighting, used to obtain better focusing effect. Therefore, weighted technology can effectively make the main peak more prominent, better location of the target.

articleTitle: Noise analysis of the triaxial piezoelectric micro-accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Noise is a major factor that constrains the performance improvement of piezoelectric micro-accelerometer in dealing with weak signals. This paper studies the noise source of piezoelectric accelerometer, which is based on theory and characteristics of noise. The background noise of the piezoelectric micro-accelerometer is composed of the mechanical thermal noise and the piezoelectric element noise. The mechanical thermal noise and noise of the piezoelectric element are modeled by the theory of thermodynamics and the noise characteristics of the integrated circuit. By modeling, analysis and calculation, it can be obtained the noise value of the mechanical thermal and the piezoelectric element are 1.53×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>μg/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> and 3.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>μg/f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> respectively.

articleTitle: Signal optimization of the AE piezoelectric sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A simple 1D model could not meet the needs of the vibration analysis of piezoelectric disk when the electromechanical couplings in the both directions of thickness and radius are strong. Using its 2-D electromechanical circuit model, we compute the response of a broadband AE sensor that is made of piezoelectric disk with small ratio of diameter and thickness. Finally, we analyze and optimize the performance of piezoelectric sensor for the Acoustic Emission (AE) applications in this paper.

articleTitle: Study on cross-sensitivity of temperature and strain of surface acoustic wave strain sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a method is proposed to solve the cross-sensitivity of strain and temperature of SAW strain sensor. In theory, the formulas of the frequency variant of resonators relate to temperature and strain are deduced by perturbation theory and the finite element method. Then the decoupling formulas to calculate the strain and temperature from two resonators' frequencies are derived. In experiment, two resonators are fabricated on Y+34°quartz substrate. the frequencies of two resonators are measured at 0°C~80°C and 0~400με. The coefficients of the above decoupling formulas are calibrated. The temperature and strain values are obtained by the frequencies of the resonators and the decoupling formulas. Compared with the referred temperature and strain in the experiment, the error of temperature is less than 2C, and the error of strain is less than 10%, which verify the feasibility of the decoupling method.

articleTitle: Studies on strain sensing properties of PVDF piezoelectric films
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: PVDF is a kind of piezoelectric film with soft texture, high sensitivity, fast response, wide frequency bandwidth and other advantages. There are few reports on the output characteristics of piezoelectric thin films under applied stress. In this paper, the sensing mechanism of PVDF piezoelectric film is analyzed theoretically. And then a numerical model set up by COMSOL software is applied to simulate the piezoelectric film. The content of the simulation is to study the variation of the output signal of the film when changing the excitation frequency, vibration amplitude and the applied stress of the exciting source. Finally, the dynamic responses of PVDF piezoelectric films with different parameters are studied experimentally. Numerical and experimental results both showed that the output signal amplitude of piezoelectric film is proportional to the amplitude of excitation, but not directly related to the external stress of the film.

articleTitle: Characterization method of flexoelectric coefficient of piezoelectrics at nanoscale
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An analytical method for measuring the flexoelectric coupling coefficient at nanoscale based on nano-compression technique is proposed in this paper. The flexoelectric formula in the method is derived through the thermodynamic method with consideration of the piezoelectric influence and the flexoelectric coupling coefficient, which can be directly obtained by measuring the stiffness of the constant cross-section pillar and the variable cross-section pillar. Meanwhile, the size and shape effect of the variable cross-section on the stiffness reduction is analyzed by numerical methods to determine the guideline for the pillars designing, hence improve the accuracy of the flexoelectric coupling coefficient measurement. The proposed method achieves flexoelectric coupling coefficient measurement at nanoscale in a mechanical way without electric polarization or current measurement, which paves the path for the design and application of the flexoelectric nano devices.

articleTitle: Simulation of wave propagation in cracked elastic medium using FDM-FEM
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Applying the finite difference method and finite element method (FDM-FEM), a methodology for handling propagating of the elastic wave is proposed. The coupling of two methods is based on the construction of a transitional zone which can pass data, assign values and eliminate the boundary effect. The practical benefits of FDM-FEM are illustrated in the simulation of wave propagating in the crack structure. Different computational domains use different methods. Hence, the simulation of wave propagation is more effective and simplifies code development and subroutines. Then, the characteristics of wave propagation are reflected through the text.

articleTitle: Investigation of incredible high performance surface acoustic wave properties with a structure of IDT/Θ0 YX-LiTaO3/SiO2/AlN/Silicon
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Recently, an Incredible High Performance (IHP) SAW structure was released by Murata Co., Ltd, which is composed by a combination of thin piezoelectric material with a Bragg reflector stack. Such structure can concentrate the energy of leaky SAW, and achieve a higher quality factor and coupling factor of SAW resonators. In this paper, we have investigated such kind of IHP SAW with a structure of IDT/ θ° YX-LiTaO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/AlN/Silicon for deep understanding of the SAWs propagating characteristics. We have calculated the relative input admittance of the IHP SAW propagating on 42° YX-LiTaO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/AlN/Silicon. We have calculated displacement filed distributions for the main and spurious modes, and evaluated the electro-mechanical coupling coefficient (K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), velocities at resonance frequency (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) and anti-resonance frequency (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>) with different electrode materials and metal thickness. Such performance was also optimized by changing the structure parameters of piezoelectric layer thickness and Euler angle.

articleTitle: Structure and electrical properties of PMN-BS-PT piezoelectric ceramics
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The structure, micromorphology, and electrical properties of the xPb(Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-(1-x)(0.3BiScO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/0.7PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) (xPMN-BS-PT, x=0.34~0.42) compositions close to the morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) have been systematically investigated as a function of PMN content (x). The phase approached from the rhombohedral toward the tetragonal phase when the PMN contents decreased. The composition with high PMN content exhibited a diffused phase transition characteristic while it showed normal ferroelectric behavior as PMN decreased. In the vicinity of the MPB, the composition (x=0.38) owned enhanced ferroelectric, piezoelectric, and electromechanical properties.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis of langasite surface acoustic wave pressure sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Langasite (La3Ga5SiO14, LGS) surface acoustic wave (SAW) pressure sensors can be applied to harsh enviroments above 500°C. The pressure sensitivity has significant effects on the accuracy of pressure measurement. The optimization of pressure sensitivity based on some factors such as substrate cuts and packaging structures has been reported. However, there is no report about the comprehensive influence of sealed cavity size and SAW sensor position on the pressure sensitivity for different cuts. In this paper, the SAW pressure sensitivity was simulated by combining the finite element method (FEM) and the perturbation theory to analyze the influence of the shape and size of sealed cavities, and sensor positions with different substrate cuts based on face pressing structure. As a result, these factors affected the sensitivity comprehensively. Thus, it is helpful to take more factors into account to improve sensitivity.

articleTitle: A gas regulator fault detecting method based on acoustic emission technology
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a new method of gas pressure regulator fault diagnosis is proposed. The wavelet packet decomposition is used for feature extraction of the acoustic emission signal. Then, based on the model obtained in the BP neural network, early regulator fault can be detected. The experimental results prove the feasibility of this method. It can effectively improve the accuracy of the fault diagnosis of the regulator. In addition, the millisecond diagnostic cycle also makes this method have a high engineering value.

articleTitle: Thickness-vibration analysis of circular AT-CUT quartz resonators partially covered with central electrodes
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Vibration frequencies and trapped modes for thickness-shear vibrations of infinite and finite partially electroded circular AT-cut quartz plates are obtained by solving the two-dimensional scalar differential equations derived by Tiersten and Smythe. The Mathieu and modified Mathieu equations are derived from the governing equation using coordinate transform and collocation method is used to deal with the boundary conditions. The current study provides a theoretical way for conducting the vibration analysis of circular quartz resonators.

articleTitle: Shear circumferential guided waves in coated gas pipeline
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Shear circumferential guide waves propagating in the gas pipeline have been widely explored in recent years. Radial cracks in gas pipeline are susceptible to shear circumferential guide waves because there are no waves conversion when ultrasonic guided waves are reflected and scattered by such defects. The development of Electromagnetic Acoustic Technique (EMAT) now can easily excite different mode of shear circumferential guide wave for crack detection. Previous investigations of guided wave propagation in the gas pipeline have led to the development of pipelines inspection for bare pipes. However, most pipes in industrial are wrapped in coatings and the existence of the coatings will bring impacts to guided waves propagation. This paper focuses on the influence of the coating on the shear circumferential guide waves in gas pipeline. Dispersion curves and distribution of energy (displacement) along the radial direction of different wave modes are discussed. The work is crucial for optimizing the parameters of EMAT transducer.

articleTitle: Stress concentration analysis of an arbitrary shape hole coated by a functionally graded layer
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on theory of the complex variable functions, the analysis of stress concentration in a homogeneous plate with an arbitrary shape hole coated by a functionally graded layer is presented. By using the method of piece-wise homogeneous layers and the technique of conformal mapping, the general solution for the functionally graded layer with normal arbitrary material properties is obtained as the plate is subjected remote uniform loads. The influences of functionally graded layer on the stress distributions around the holes with various shapes such as triangle, square, rectangle etc. are discussed in detail by numerical examples. It is shown that the stress concentration around an arbitrary shape hole can be successfully decreased by choosing proper change ways of elastic modulus along normal direction in the layer. The results for some special cases are compared with previous literatures and found in good agreement.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric characterization of Ca2Al2SiO7 crystals
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: High temperature piezoelectric crystal materials are promising for various applications especially the sensors serving under harsh environment without failure for structural health monitoring and/or nondestructive evaluation of the modern aerospace structures at elevated temperatures (above 600<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C). The Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub> (CAS) is a newly developed piezoelectric crystal. In this report, the dielectric, piezoelectric and electromechanical properties of CAS crystal grown by Czochralski pulling method were evaluated by means of impedance method. The independent piezoelectric coefficients d14 and d36 at room temperature were determined to be on the order of 6.7 and 2.8pC/N, respectively. For potential piezoelectric sensor application, the maximum piezoelectric coefficients of d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26</sub> were calculated, where the largest du value was obtained to be 3.1 pC/N for (XYtl)45°/-55° crystal cut, and the largest piezoelectric d26 was found to be 4.7 pC/N for (YXl)45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> crystal cut, which is nearly two times that of alpha quartz. Moreover, the temperature dependence of piezoelectric coefficients of CAS crystal were obtained to show small variations (2%~6%) from ambient temperature to 700<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, indicating the advantages of CAS crystal for high temperature piezoelectric application.

articleTitle: Rayleigh waves in functionally graded material half-space by orthogonal polynomial method
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This work presents a theoretical study of the propagation characteristics of Rayleigh waves in functionally graded material (FGM) half-space. Based on the three-dimensional linear elasticity theory, Rayleigh waves in FGM half-space are investigated by using the Laguerre orthogonal polynomial method. In the present paper, the dispersion curves, displacement and stress distributions of FGM half-space are illustrated. Results are compared with reference published earlier to check up the accuracy of the Laguerre polynomial method. The effects of gradient variation of material constants on phase velocity dispersion curves, displacement and stress distributions curves are analysed in detail.

articleTitle: A piezoelectric wind energy harvesting device with right-angle cantilever beam
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Energy utilization and environment protection are universal hot topics in our society. Harvesting ambient clean energy sources to supply low power devices has shown a wide application potential. In this paper, a kind of right-angle piezoelectric cantilever beam is proposed to harvesting wind energy as a power supplier for remote wireless sensor network nodes. Structure design and working principle of the device are introduced. Performances of the device are investigated numerically and experimentally, which are compared with the traditional cantilever beam. The strain distributions and natural frequencies of the structures are analyzed with FEA simulations. With the same natural frequency and piezoelectric element, output capacities of the prototypes were tested under different wind speeds. With an optimal load of about 500 kΩ, the maximum output power of the right-angle cantilever beam is over 1.3mW under the wind speed of 6 m/s, which is about twice as much as the traditional cantilever beam.

articleTitle: A Novel surface acoustic wave DMMP sensor coated with Zinc oxide quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Currently, many surface acoustic wave (SAW) gas sensors coated with Zinc oxide (ZnO), have high operating temperature and poor sensitivity for dimethyl methyl phosphonate (DMMP). Thus, we fabricate a novel SAW gas sensor to detect the DMMP at room temperature. Due to the excellent solution processability, low cost and ease of integration, quantum dots (QDs) are emerging as promising candidates for gas sensors. Zinc oxide quantum dots (ZnO QDs) were synthesized by using a succinct colloidal method. In order to construct gas sensors, ZnO QDs were drop-coated onto 128°YX LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> piezoelectric substrates. A differential SAW oscillator with excellent frequency stability was performed and a delay-line SAW resonator with low insertion loss was designed as the feedback element of the oscillator. Large sensor response and good repeatability were observed in the experiments at 25 °C. The detection limit and measured sensitivity were evaluated as 0.13 ppm and 46.4 Hz/ppm, respectively.

articleTitle: Vibrations of perforated beams filled with fluids
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A theoretical study on natural frequencies and mode shapes of perforated beams filled with ideal fluids is presented. In the analysis, it is assumed that the beams are simply supported at both ends. The Rayleigh - Ritz method is used for the accurate analysis of perforated beams with different patterns of hole and fluids. The accuracy is improved with the increase of order of displacement functions, and satisfactory results are obtained. The results have also been verified by observing a good agreement with earlier results and the finite element analysis. The analysis is intended for applications of piezoelectric inkjet printerhead structures.

articleTitle: Analysis on saw device of LiNbO3 film with multi-layered media
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation of the surface acoustic wave (SAW) in LiNbO3 structure with multi-layered media is introduced. The SAW devices with LiNbO3 structure are simulated by finite element methods, symmetry and anti-symmetry resonance modes of vibration with the corresponding resonant frequency are obtained. The effects of interdigital transducer (IDT)parameters on the performance of the device are analyzed; the changes in resonance frequency of SAW device due to the electrical loading are studied for various metallization ratios and thickness of the interdigital transducer. According to the simulation results and technological conditions, the optimum parameters areselected for the design of the gas sensor. With the concentration - frequency coefficient is approximately 1.412 ppm/Hz, which has an excellent linear relationship.

articleTitle: Finite element modelling of macro fiber composite with interdigitated electrode for engineering applications
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Smart structures with Macro fiber composite (MFC) piezoelectric actuators have been increasingly applied in engineering. A simple but elaborate finite element model of the smart structures not only can predict vibration dynamics, but also can reduce challenges and computational expense in engineering application. Therefore, a simplified FEM developed to model MFC with interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) is proposed in this paper. A new scheme of FEM for IDEs in MFC is presented. With assuming the poling direction is along the same direction and voltage-progressive electrodes configuration in FEM, the piezoelectric elements employ an equivalent periodic tensile/compressive strain and constant electric potential in the poling direction. Numerical tests of free strain and blocking force and experimental methods are both employed to verify the FEM in this paper. A cantilever aluminum beam with a single MFC actuator is presented. The natural frequencies, vertical deflection and Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC) based on the resonant frequencies show the fidelity of the EF model agree well with experimental measurement. This work presented provides a novel FEM to model MFC for engineering applications such as vibration actuation.

articleTitle: The influence of maxwell stress on the periodical cracks in piezoelectric material
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The effects of Maxwell stress on semi-permeable periodical cracks in piezoelectric material under combined mechanical and electric loadings at infinity is studied. Based on the extended Stroh formalism, the closed-form expression of electric displacement in cracks, the stress and electrostatic fields and field intensity factors are obtained in a concise way. Numerical results are given to discuss the effects of Maxwell stress on the stress and electric displacement intensity factors with increasing remote loadings. Additionally, we find that when relatively big period (over four times the crack length) is adopted, one can obtain similar solutions from the case of a single crack.

articleTitle: Effect of porous and segregation defects on the mechanical properties of magnesium alloy
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Magnesium alloy as a new type of alloy material enjoys some excellent properties, but it always inevitably generates some kind of defects, such as porous, bubble, inclusion and segregation defects. Defects seriously impact the mechanical properties of magnesium alloy, therefore, the study of defects is important. In this paper, we analyzed the effect of porous and segregation defects on the property of magnesium alloy by experimenting. Through the experiment of different percentage of defects, we can compare the influence of defects content to mechanical properties of alloy. It has also developed a high temperature experiments, which can test the impact of high temperature on the defects and alloys. The microstructures of segregation and porous tissues were analyzed, from the segregation and porous structural characteristics, we analyzed the reason why material degradation and damage patterns. And discusses its formation mechanism and prevention measures.

articleTitle: Controllable preparation of ultralong ZnO nanowire arrays based on microfluidics
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, hydrothermal method is combined with microfluidic technology to fabricate a microfluidic chip for the controllable preparation of ultralong ZnO nanowire arrays (ZNAs). First, the existing technical proposals and experimental parameters are optimized. Then, the seed solution is injected into the microchannel of microfluidic chip to form a dense ZnO seed layer. Finally, the growth solution is injected to prepare ZNAs on the surface of the ZnO seed layer in the microchannel. X-ray diffraction result shows that the as-prepared ZNAs possess high crystallinity and exhibit a preferred growth orientation along the c-axis. In addition, scanning electron microscopy images show that the length of ZNA reaches up to 46 μm by appropriately controlling the growth temperature (90 C), flow rate (15 μL/min) and growth time (10 h), which effectively increases the growth rate of ZNA.

articleTitle: The interaction of highly nonlinear solitary waves and viscoelastic half-space
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The method of nondestructive testing (NDT) using the coupling of highly nonlinear solitary waves in one-dimensional particle chains and structures is a new research hotspot which is gradually improved. Based on properties of solitary wave, we investigate the coupling mechanism between highly nonlinear solitary waves and viscoelastic half-space and obtain the complete coupling differential equation system. By solving the equations with Runge-Kutta method and analyzing the reflected wave, we find that reflected solitary waves are sensitive especially to the Young's module and viscosity of the viscoelastic half-space. These findings can be applied to the NDT to the material properties of viscoelastic structures and it also enrich the theory of solitary wave flaw detection.

articleTitle: Research on the multi-physics simulation and chip implementation of piezoelectric contour mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper introduces the operating principles of a piezoelectric contour-mode resonators, and analyzes the resonance process through multi-physics finite element analysis method. Compared with Modified Butterworth-Van-Dyke model equivalent circuit designed piezoelectric resonator, the multi-physics simulation can analyze the influence of each component on resonator performance, such as dimensions of resonator fixed position and thickness of upper and lower electrodes. The 140MHz contour mode resonator is designed based on the simulation and optimization results, and produced through MEMS technology; the test results indicate that the resonator possesses a higher Q value with an electromechanical coupling coefficient of 2%, which is basically consistent with the simulation results. The 140MHz contour mode filter is designed based on the resonator with a 3db bandwidth of 1MHz and a center insertion loss of 3.5db, which has a high rectangle coefficient and out-band suppression up to50db.

articleTitle: Growth and piezoelectric properties of Sr3Ta(Al0.5Ga0.5)3Si2O14 crystals with langasite structure
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: New piezoelectric crystal Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ta(Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub> (STAGS) with ordered langasite structure was successfully grown by Czochralski method. The lattice parameters of STAGS were a = 8.269 Å, c = 5.036 Å. The rocking curve evident the crystal quality declined and the diffraction peak shift slightly from top to bottom. Element analysis revealed the Al<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> was not easy to occupy the C site as Ga<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in crystal. The piezoelectric coefficients d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of STAGS was found to be 5.1pC/N and the resistivity was high up to 4.94×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Ω·m for top part and 7.08×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Ω·cm for bottom part at 700°C, respectively.

articleTitle: Structural dynamics modeling and experimental study of axially precompressed piezoelectric bimorph
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric bimorph has many advantages such as light weight, small volume and no electromagnetic interference. It has a very significant advantage in the application of MAV and intelligent ammunition rudder control. The axial force can effectively improve the output performance and the electromechanical conversion efficiency of the bimorph. In order to provide theoretical basis for structural design and parameter optimization of axial compression bimorph, based on the assumption of Bernoulli-Euler beam, a structural dynamic model of axial compression bimorph was established based on Hamiltonian principle. Then, the static deformation, the natural vibration, the amplitude-frequency characteristic and the buckling critical load of the bimorph were deduced. Then the calculated results of the above model were compared with ANSYS simulation results and test results to verify the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the performance of microflown with SHS configuration
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, the microflown with SHS configuration is analyzed by numerical simulation. Compared to conventional acoustic sensors, microflown measures the particle velocity rather than the sound pressure. It has three resistors, two outermost resistors of which are used as sensors, while the resistor located in the middle is used as a heater. As air flows across the sensor, upstream resistor cools down and gives off some heat to the passing air. Hence, downstream resistors lose less heat because the warmer air passes through. The temperature difference can be calculated and analyzed by assuming the ideal circuit structure for the microflown with SHS configuration, respectively.

articleTitle: Least square smoothing algorithm and gauss decomposition spectral analysis method in spectral gamma ray logging
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In the exploration of deep mineral resources, natural gamma spectrometer logging technology is a method which can realizes qualitative and quantitative analysis of deep underground radioactive elements. However, the low energy resolution of natural gamma ray spectrometry logging results in low reliability of distinguishing the radioactive element, therefore the study of spectral analysis method is particularly important. In this paper, the least square smoothing algorithm and the Gauss decomposition method are studied. The results show that the third order polynomial with 5 points smooth window has a good smoothing effect on the spectral data. The spectrum processed by using of the Gauss decomposition method is affected by the separation degree and the peak to height ratio. It is fast and accurate to choose the Gauss decomposition method to solve the spectral data when the separation degree of overlapping peaks is greater than 0.4, and the difference of peak heights are large. This paper provides the basis for the application and selection of the generally analytical method in the actual logging processing, which is of great significance.

articleTitle: Electroless deposition nickel on piezoelectric ceramic PZT
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The Ni/Pb(Zr, Ti)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Ni trilayers have been prepared by electroless deposition. The structure of Ni deposited onto PZT with various crystal cuts is evaluated by X-ray diffraction (XRD). The cross-section of the Ni/PZT/Ni trilayers are investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The characterization and quantification of the elements are carried out using an energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS). The friction, film hardness and elastic modulus of the structure are characterized by Micro Material Nano Test Vantage. The structure hysteresis loop is tested through the magneto-electric-elastic coupling coefficients test system. The best experimental conditions can be found in this article by changing the pH value and reducing agent.

articleTitle: Design and experimental research on preamplifier module for PVDF piezoelectric film sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: PVDF is a polymer formed by the monomer partial fluorine ethylene CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = CF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> polymerization. It has good piezoelectric effect and is widely used in vibration measurement and other fields. In this paper, by analyzing the circuit model of PVDF piezoelectric thin film, the preamplifier module is designed, analyzed theoretically and tested. Testing results are consistent with theoretical ones. The flow field information of the circular tube was tested by the preamplifier module of the PVDF piezoelectric film sensors. Experimental results show that when measuring tube flow in low frequency region, PVDF piezoelectric film sensors are much better than accelerometer sensors. It can measure abundant low-frequency components, which provides a good experimental basis for analyzing the flow field in the tube.

articleTitle: Research on a cryogenic micro-displacement piezoelectric actuator for the radio telescope panels
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on the merits of ultrasonic motors, a micro-displacement actuator driven by an ultrasonic motor for the radio telescope panels is presented. The whole system includes mechanical structure and motion control unit. In the mechanical structure, the traveling wave rotary ultrasonic motor is used to drive the actuator. The transmission part adopts a differential thread shaft to converts the rotational displacement of the motor into the linear micro-displacement of the driving end and improve the accuracy of micro-displacement. The whole structure is sealed with metal foils so that no humid air could come into the structure inside. The core of the motion control is the DSP and ultrasonic motor driving circuit. Environmental simulation experiments are carried out and the results show that the stepping precision of the actuator can reach 1μm at both room temperature and minus 40 degrees Celsius. The prototype shows good characteristics when working in humid air and under low temperature. The presented actuator can work properly in the environment of Antarctic.

articleTitle: Temperature and potential fields of an interface crack in thermoelectric dual materials
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The temperature and potential field problems of an interfacial crack in thermoelectric dual materials is studied in this research. The main solution is derived based on the complex variable method. Thermoelectric materials subjected to remote electric current and energy flow, the solutions of temperature and electric potential on the interface crack surface are obtained in closed-form. Finally, the fields of electric current, energy flow at the crack tip are discussed.

articleTitle: Discrete element numerical simulation on rutting deformation of asphalt mixture
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Discrete element method was used to investigate the rutting depth variation of asphalt mixture under the condition of different aggregate gradation, varying loads and varying temperatures. The results indicate that for either gap gradation or continuous gradation asphalt mixture, when the content of coarse aggregate is the same, the ability to resist rutting deformation of specimens enhances when the maximum nominal size increases, and when the maximum nominal size is the same, the ability of the latter is superior to the former. Rutting depths with different loading sequences are similar. For the same average load, rutting depths are close. When the average temperature is the same, rutting depths are very close when the temperature changes from low to high or from high to low.

articleTitle: On the measuring circuit of piezoelectric accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Due to its excellent dynamic performance for vibration measurement, MEMS-based piezoelectric accelerometer has been studied in recent years. Piezoelectric micro-accelerometer can be regarded as a component that can produce electric charge with high internal impedance, but the quantity of electric charge is very subtle. By taking this into account, the general measuring circuit does not meet the requirement. In this paper, a charge amplifier with an integrated chip is used instead of a large number of discrete components, and cold-discharge design is also included to decrease the thermal noise of the whole circuit.

articleTitle: Research on the parametric array's acoustic characteristics in layered medium
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The parametric array can eradiate high directivity, low frequency beams with a small aperture, so it has gained wide attention in underwater acoustic engineering. Meanwhile, the parametric array's conversion efficiency is very low, severely restrict the parametric array's further application. In order to improve the conversion efficiency, this report used the KZK equation to calculate the parametric array's acoustic characteristics in the layered medium. Results showed that the maximum values of the difference wave always appeared at the junction of the layered medium, and the layered medium with larger nonlinear parameter, smaller velocity and lower attenuation coefficient has a larger conversion efficiency. The report may provide theoretical guidance for the parametric array's future applications.

articleTitle: Discrimination of echo signal of acoustic surface wave resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator measuring technology can be applied in realizing wireless passive parameter detection even with the environment of high temperature, high pressure, strong electromagnetic radiation and strong electromagnetic radiation interference. However, in the channel transmission, the signal is inevitably interfered and the shaded and shielded signal will appear, which is fatal to the parameter determination of the acoustic surface wave resonant echo. In order to avoid the error of output parameters, According to the time domain characteristics of surface acoustic wave echo signal, we proposed a signal screening methods(the surface acoustic wave resonance echo signal time domain method of screening), this method does not need to establish complex mathematical model, and it is simply effectively and timely to distinguish the error signal(the interfering signal and the shaded and shielded signal). The simulation results show that this method can accurately isolation the signal of low signal-to-noise ratio. Finally, the accuracy of the method is proved by the wireless passive SAW temperature sensing experiment.

articleTitle: Rapidly measuring elastic coefficients of new piezoelectric materials using resonant ultrasound spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The growing demand for new material characterization has become the driving force behind the development of resonant ultrasound spectroscopy(RUS). Due to the irregular shape or the layered structure of new materials, the use of finite element method(FEM) instead of Rayleigh-Ritz model to calculate the intrinsic vibration mode has gradually become a trend. In the usual FEM, the resonance spectrum is usually calculated by the frequency domain response method, which includes the intrinsic frequency and amplitude of resonance pulses. However, the calculation takes too much of time, and the process of measuring elastic material constants is rather long. In order to further shorten the measurement time, only the eigenfrequency is calculated using FEM in this paper, and then take measured frequencies and computed frequencies into comparison. A probability matching method is proposed. In the experimental section, taking the new piezoelectric material CNA0.5G0.5S (CNAGS) as an example, which verifies the modal probability matching method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis on performance of flextensional piezoelectric hydrophone
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A theoretical model of flextensional piezoelectric hydrophone (FPH) is proposed to meet the requirements of high sensitivity and low frequency. The FPH is two circular piezoelectric layers with a laminated structure. Two kinds of the connection forms of the two piezoelectric plates, in series and in parallel, have been studied. The effect of geometrical parameters, thickness and radius, on the detection performance has been investigated to improve sensitivity of the FPH around the low frequency range. Moreover, the theoretical results are verified by finite element method. Moreover, the theoretical solutions under geometric optimization are obtained. The results provide a theoretical basis for design of the FPH.

articleTitle: Joint damage identification for a steel frame using compression sensing-based EMI signatures
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An experimental study of damage identification for a three-layered steel frame is implemented. Damages are introduced by completely loosening bolts over several conditions on the structure and then the piezoelectric admittance signatures are obtained under various damage locations. EMI signatures are pre-processed using the theory of compression sensing and the compressed signatures still keep the original damage information invariable. Finally, the principal components of the compressed EMI signatures are obtained as the input parameters of BP neural network for quantitative damage identification. Research shows that the transmission bandwidth and storage space of the processed data are reduced greatly using the compression perception technique, and the present hybrid method can detect the damage locations quantitatively.

articleTitle: Characteristics of surface acoustic waves based on (110)ZNO/(110)ALN/R-sapphire structure
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of Love waves in (110)ZnO/(110)AlN/R-sapphire structure are theoretically investigated by 3-dimensional finite element method (3D FEM). The phase velocity v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sub>, coupling coefficient k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of the first two orders of Love wave are calculated, in which the thicknesses of (110) ZnO and (110) AlN are varied. The results show that the 0th Love wave has the largest coupling coefficient, and at H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ALN</sub>/λ=0.37 and h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">zno</sub>=3.4 μm, the maximum k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 4.27% associated with Vp of 3773 m/s and TCF of -22.1 ppm/°C can be obtained. Simulation results indicate that the (110)ZnO/(110)AlN/R-sapphire structure exhibits high phase velocity, large coupling coefficient and small TCF, which can be used for designing the high-frequency and temperature-compensated SAW devices.

articleTitle: Love waves propagating in a PMN-0.29PT single crystal layer on a piezomagnetic substrate with an imperfect interface
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: We investigate the dispersion behaviors of Love waves in the coupled structure which consists of a piezomagnetic substrate and PMN-0.29PT layer with different cut orientations in this paper. The layered structure with an imperfectly bonded interface, and the interface imperfection is described by the linear spring model. The surfaces of the structure are free of traction, electrically shorted or open. The numerical examples are given to illustrate the effects of the electrical boundary conditions, the imperfect interface parameters, and the PMN-0.29PT cut orientations on the dispersion behaviors.

articleTitle: Study of anisotropy evaluation using cross-dipole acoustic LWD
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The evaluation of anisotropy is one of the key and difficult points in the study of acoustic logging while drilling(AWLD). In this paper, the finite different method(FDM) is used to simulate the acoustic field excited by the cross-dipole sources in the anisotropic formation. And the flexural waves excited by dipole sources are used to invert the formation anisotropy in the ALWD. The results show that the cross-dipole sources in the HTI formation will stimulate the fast and the slow flexural waves whose velocities are less than these of the fast and the slow shear wave respectively. While using these two flexural waves, we managed to evaluate the anisotropy with a least squares fitting method based on analytic method. Moreover, the transverse direction of the transverse shear wave is obtained by the orthogonal component inversed by the Alford four component method.

articleTitle: The simulation design of low frequency broadband transmit-receive transducer with composite fluid cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A design of underwater transducer with composite cavity structure is presented. This transducer adopts piezoelectric ceramic tubes and a larger metal tube forming a composite fluid cavity. While working in the water, the transducer possesses multiple fluid cavity vibration modes which expand the bandwidth of the transducer. FEM calculation results show that, the transducer can work well both as a transmitting transducer and as a hydrophone in a bandwidth of two octaves as long as the structure sizes were reasonably designed. This new structure transducer possesses the characteristics of low frequency, broadband and transmit-receive using.

articleTitle: Structural optimization of partially ring-electroded ZnO thin film resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A design of ring electrode deposited on a rectangular ZnO thin film is proposed in this paper to demonstrate the existence of a nearly uniform displacement distribution at the central part of this kind of resonators. A variational formulation constructed based on a scalar equation provides a theoretical basis for Ritz method in our analysis. The mode shapes of the fundamental thickness-stretch mode of this ring-electroded resonator are obtained. The structural parameters of the ring electrode are optimized in order to achieve a relatively flat vibration region, which guarantees a higher accuracy and repeatable measurement for sensing detection in an air or liquid environment. These results can provide a fundamental reference of the design and optimization of structural parameters of a high quality sensor.

articleTitle: The influence of bias magnetic field on the frequency of magnetoelectric composite materials
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents an speed measurement method based on the magnetoelectric (ME) materials which response to the magnetic field. A theoretical analysis was conducted on the principle of rotation speed measurement and a numerical analysis on the ME device response the magnetic field using different material size is performed. Numerical calculation results show that when the Young's modulus varies with the magnetic field, the characteristic frequency of ME materials response varies periodically. The rotation speed counting method develops by searching the maximum output voltage of ME device. The ME rotation speed measurement system is set up and ME device with high performance is fabricated on the ME materials. Experimental results verify the validity and feasibility of presented rotation speed measurement method.

articleTitle: Surface shear interface waves in a prestressed piezoelectric layered structure
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: To automatically actualize ultrasonic nondestructive testing applications for structures with subsurface damage, we investigate horizontal shear interface waves in a prestressed piezoelectric layered structure. The elastic material with subsurface gradient damage can be considered as a structure in an elastic half-space covered by a gradient layer, and the upper covered piezoelectric layer can be considered as a piezoelectric half-space. We derive the field control equations with respect to the displacement function and the electrical potential function, and we solve the equations by the power series method. The results show that horizontal shear interface waves can propagate in this structure. The relation between wave number and wave velocity and the distribution of displacement amplitude, potential amplitude, and stress amplitude are illustrated. Numerical examples reveal the horizontal shear interface wave to have a normal dispersion. The more serious the subsurface damage is, the lower the phase velocity is. The method presented and the conclusions herein can provide a theoretical basis for ultrasonic nondestructive testing.

articleTitle: Research of active control based on two kinds of acoustic separation methods
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The effect of traditional passive sound absorption material on low-frequency sound waves is limited. So, the active control method is put forward to eliminate the echo of low-frequency. But in the sound field, the incident wave and the reflected wave are superimposing together, we need to isolate the incident wave and the reflected wave in order to control the reflected wave. In this paper, we present two methods of isolating the incident wave and the reflected wave in the sound fields, the two methods are double-pressure sensor method and pressure-velocity sensor method. And the two kinds of acoustic separation methods are used to simulate and analyze the active control of reflected wave.

articleTitle: A multi-channel a-scan ultrasound system for real-time, non-invasive study of carotid artery compliance
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the most common causes of death in the world, while the compliance of carotid artery is an important parameter for predicting cardiovascular disease. Current methods of carotid artery compliance evaluation include B-mode scanners or single channel A-mode scanner. The B-mode scanner method needs extensive image processing algorithms and the cost is expensive, while the single channel A-mode scanner method easily results in huge measurement errors. To solve these problems, an eight-channel A-mode ultrasound system for carotid artery compliance measuring was invented. The system was tested by the carotid phantom models and its accuracy was compared with the single channel A-mode and B-mode scanner. Our Result shows that this eight channel A-mode system could measure the carotid compliance accurately and could be an alternative for the B-mode scanner.

articleTitle: A study of single piezoelectric fiber frictional sliding during loading and unloading process
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The efficiency of load transfer across the interface of piezoelectric fiber and matrix plays a significant role on the mechanical behavior of piezoelectric fiber composites. In the debonding region, Frictional sliding is the main mode of the load transfer. Several experimental tests are designed to measure the frictional properties of piezoelectric composite between matrix and piezoelectric. In the unloading process, there is only frictional sliding and no new debonding occurs. That's to say, we can obtain the frictional coefficient through the analysis of unloading process, the purpose of the present study is to extend the application of the single-fiber pullout test to evaluating the interfacial and frictional properties of piezoelectric composite between matrix and piezoelectric fiber.

articleTitle: Analysis on the interaction of two micro-beams immersed in liquid upper a quartz crystal plate and the induced frequency shift
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The coupled dynamic model of a QCR carrying an array of micro-beams in liquid environment is established. The flow velocity distribution around single beam and double beams are compared and analyzed. The results show that for a sparse array of micro-beams, the results of a single beam can be applied to all beams if the vibration states of each beam are assumed to be consistent. As an example, the frequency shift induced by a sparse array of micro-beams immersed in liquid is calculated. It is revealed that the influence of liquid on micro-beams is added mass effect.

articleTitle: Effect of electrode width on the sensitivity of the surface acoustic wave detector in a GC/SAW
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper analyzes the effect of electrode width on the sensitivity of the surface acoustic wave (SAW) detector in a GC/SAW. By using the finite element method (FEM) and the COMSOL software, the coupling-of-modes (COM) parameters of the SAW detector with different electrode width are quickly and accurately extracted. Based on the COM model and P-matrix cascading technique, the frequency responses of the detector are simulated with different electrode width and the sensitivity of the SAW detector corresponding to the different width of the IDT are obtained. The theoretical results provide the foundation for further experimental research.

articleTitle: Lattice scale study of the interaction between the vortex and anti-vortex polarization domain
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on the long-range potential of the shell model at atomic scale, the interaction between polarization vectors has been obtained at lattice scale. Under the assumption of the domain structure constitution, the interaction between the vortex and anti-vortex with different combinations has been delivered. From the interaction, it can be found that the interaction between the vortex and anti-vortex has attraction property. And the limitation distance between vortex and anti-vortex must greater than one lattice. These results will give some new views about the interaction of the domain pattern in the ferroelectric.

articleTitle: Solution of an infinite piezoelectric matrix containing a circular inclusion with an elliptic hole
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This work mainly focused on the problem of an infinite piezoelectric matrix containing a circular inclusion with an elliptic hole under remote loadings. By using complex variable method, conformal transformation and Fourier expansion, the influence of material constant proportion between matrix and inclusion, as well as the eccentric distance of the elliptic hole on stress and electric displacement field is investigated. In this paper, the explicit and analytic results are given, which can provide scientific basis for getting optimal stress distribution by controlling the position of defect and optimizing the material constant proportion to lower the risk of fracture failure.

articleTitle: Simulation of surface acoustic wave propagating characteristics in relaxor based ferroelectric single crystals poled along [011]
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of surface acoustic waves (SAWs) on Y-cut X propagating Pb(In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Pb(Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-xPbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (PIN-PMN-xPT) substrates with different PT composition (x=0.28 and 0.32) were theoretically analyzed. The calculated results indicated existence of a shear horizontal (SH) SAW with ultrahigh electromechanical coupling factor K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The variation of SAWs properties with rotated Euler angle θ was also investigated. The largest K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for the SH SAW could reach 60% when θ=45°. The K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for the SH SAW with different PT contents was calculated, and it was found that the K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for the 0.32PT substrate was larger than that for 0.28PT substrate. The influence of Mn-doping on SAW properties for YX-PIN-PMN-0.28PT substrate was also analyzed. The simulated results showed that after Mn-doping the velocity increased while the K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> decreased, which confirmed the phenomenon of “hard” effect caused by Mn-doping.

articleTitle: Electroelastic analysis of functionally graded one-dimensioanl quasicrystal plates
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Three-dimensional electroelastic analysis is presented for functionally graded one-dimensional quasicrystal plates with four lateral sides being simply supported. The functionally graded material properties are assumed to be exponentially distributed along the thickness direction. Based on the pseudo-Stroh formalism, the exact solution for functionally graded one-dimensional piezoelectric quasicrystal plates is derived. The obtained solution is subsequently applied to study the functionally graded exponential factor influence on physical quantities in the phonon, phason and electric fields of the plates subjected to a z-direction top surface mechanical load. Numerical results can be used as the benchmark results for assessing the accuracy of other numerical methods.

articleTitle: A piezoelectric energy harvester based on a piezoelectric beam with a ferroelectric inversion layer
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexural vibration of piezoelectric beam with a ferroelectric inversion layer is analyzed. The structure analyzed represents a kind of piezoelectric generator for converting mechanical energy from Flexural vibrations to electrical energy. Analytical expressions and numerical results for the output voltage, current, power, efficiency and power density are given.

articleTitle: Study on characteristics of surface acoustic wave based on (110)ScAlN/R-sapphire structrue
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of surface acoustic wave (SAW) in IDT/(110)ScAlN/R-sapphire, including the Rayleigh wave propagating along [001] direction and Love wave propagating along [100] direction, are investigated by 3 dimension-finite element method (3D-FEM). The phase velocity (v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>), electromechanical coupling coefficient (k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and mass sensitivity (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>) of first two orders of Rayleigh wave and Love wave are calculated. The simulated results show that the mode 0 of SAWs has better performances than that of mode 1. The mode 0 of Rayleigh wave shows the maximum k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 3.57% as h/λ=1 associated with v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> of 3676 m/s and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> of 23.6 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/kg; and the mode 0 of Love wave exhibits the maximum k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 6.39% as h/λ=0.33 associated with v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> of 4644 m/s and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> of 38.3 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/kg. The results indicate that (110)ScAlN/R-sapphire structure can be used for the fabrication of SAW devices with high frequency and good sensitivity.

articleTitle: Investigation of properites of PIN-PMN-PT single crystal and its high performance application for a piezoelectric energy harvester
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The relaxor-based ferroelectric single crystal Pb(In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Pb(Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (PIMNT) were grown successfully by the vertical Bridgman techique using the [0 0 1]-oriented seed, then the test behavior of dielectric and piezoelectric under hydrostatic pressure were performed by measuring the capacitance, dissipation and resonance frequency, antiresonance frequency of the [0 0 1]-oriented PIMNT, respectively. In order to research the application of ferroelectric single crystal on piezoelectric energy harvester. We employ the piezoelectric bimorph model and change the piezoelectric material from PZT-5H to PIMNT, and we find that the maximum output power density increased when the piezoelectric material change from PZT-5H to PIMNT, we note that the ferroelectric material, such as PIM-PMN-PT, can substantially decrease the resonant frequency of the system compare with that of the PZT-5H. In addition, we investgated the relationship between efficiency and input frequency for different piezoelectric layer. These findings can provide gudiance to design Piezoelectric Energy Harvester.

articleTitle: Surface energy effect on free vibration behavior of the piezoelectric cylindrical nanoshell
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, free vibration analysis of the piezoelectric cylindrical nanoshell is studied based on electro-elastic surface/interface theory. Some fundamental formulations are first given to obtain the total energy of the nanoshell. Then the natural frequency is derived from Rayleigh-Ritz energy method. Finally, some numerical examples are presented to analyze the effect of surface parameter and applied voltage on the natural frequency of the piezoelectric nanoshell.

articleTitle: Excitation and propagation of flexural plate wave
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexural plate wave (FPW) can be used to detect the crack on the plate, so investigating the excitation and propagation characteristics of FPW becomes particularly important and urgent. Effective methods to generate FPW are researched by transducers arrangement. The experimental dispersion curves of FPW were measured by incremental distance measurements using laser vibrometer, and is compared with the theoretical curves. The experiment shows that the FPW can be excited more effectively by using two transducers with the distance of one wavelength. The experimental dispersion curves of the phase and group velocity of FPW are in agreement with the theoretical curves.

articleTitle: Investigation of the radial extensional mode of ln piezoelectric crystal
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric materials functional at elevated temperatures without failure are desirable for various piezoelectric applications. In this paper, the lithium niobate (LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, LN) crystal and the radial extensional (RE) properties were studied. Based on the crystal symmetry, the equations to evaluate the k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> value with Z- and Y-oriented discs were deduced. Using the deduced equations, the k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> values of the Z-oriented and Y-oriented LN crystal discs were calculated and obtained to be 3.83% and 24.7%, respectively. In addition, the radial extension mode was studied experimentally by impedance method, where the k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> values were found to be on the order of 3.80% and 24.5%, respectively. Moreover, the temperature dependence of RE electromechanical properties were investigated from room temperature to 500°C, where the variation of the k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> was found to be <;8% for the Y-oriented discs. The large k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> value and minimal temperature dependent behavior of Y-oriented crystal cuts indicating the potential uses for high temperature piezoelectric application.

articleTitle: Surface motion of anisotropic half space containing different defects under plane SH wave
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Surface motion of anisotropic half space under plane SH wave is investigated by means of complex function method and multi polar coordinate system. The anisotropy of the half space is considered in order to satisfy practical condition. Three defects (cavity, inclusion and lining) are discussed to demonstrate different influences on surface motion. Based on different boundary conditions of defects, surface displacement amplitudes of the half space under plane SH wave are investigated. Numerical results show that surface motion of the half space is affected by the defect embedded significantly, especially when the half space is anisotropic.

articleTitle: Multifield simulation and experiment of electromagnetic acoustic transducers
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An FEM model is proposed for the generation of Lamb wave using meander-line-coil electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs). We aim to investigate the contribution of dynamic electromagnetic field to generate Lamb wave in EMATs operating on the Lorenz principle. The EMAT model was described by static magnetic field, dynamic electromagnetic field, eddy current, Lorenz force, and displacement. First, the bias magnetic field by permanent magnet was simulated to generate Lamb wave. Secondly, the influence of dynamic electromagnetic field on the excitation process of Lamb wave was discussed in detail. Thirdly, a Lamb wave dispersion curve in frequency-wavenumber domain was plot by using 2D Fourier transform. The simulation and experiment results show that the dynamic magnetic field does not contribute to the excitation of the Lamb wave, and the influence of the dynamic magnetic field can be ignored in the modeling of the EMATs.

articleTitle: Influence of surface micro-beams with large deflection on the frequency shift of a quartz resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper studies the nonlinear effect of the composite quartz crystal resonator system. A vibration equation considering the nonlinear deformation effect of micro-beams is established, and then the perturbation solution of the vibration equation is solved. Frequency shift of the compound quartz crystal resonator system depends on material and geometrical parameters is illustrated for nonlinear and linear vibration. It is found that the frequency shift produces a little right (or left) translation for increasing elastic modulus (or aspect ratio) of micro-beams when taking into account the nonlinear effect of the MBs.

articleTitle: Energy reflection and transmission characteristics of longitudinal wave in multilayer structure
publicationTitle: 2017 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The study on the energy reflection and transmission mechanism of ultrasonic waves in adhesive structures is very important. In view of this issue, the interaction between the ultrasound and the interface under the longitudinal wave incidence at different angles was discussed when the plate-like adhesive structure interface was intact. Besides, the influence of the change in frequency-thickness product on the energy reflection and transmission characteristics of sound wave was analyzed. The numerical results showed that the wave conversion does not occur when the longitudinal wave is incident perpendicularly, and the obvious periodic resonance appears in the energy reflection and transmission coefficient curve of longitudinal wave with the increase of frequency-thickness product.
